title: Standard deviation
examples: How does standard deviation tell me if the data is spread out?
If I change one number, how much does the standard deviation change?

explain.say: Today we learn about standard deviation. It measures how spread out your data is. A small standard deviation means data points are close together. A large standard deviation means data points are far apart.
We use a calculator to find this value easily. You enter your set of numbers into the statistics mode. Then you select the standard deviation function to calculate it.
If you change one number in the data set, the standard deviation changes. Changing a number far from the average increases the spread. Changing it close to the average decreases the spread.
Consider two groups of test scores. One group has scores like ninety, ninety, ninety. The other has scores like seventy, eighty, one hundred. The second group has a larger standard deviation.

faq.q: What does a low standard deviation mean for my data?
faq.a: It means your data points are very close to the average value. The data is quite consistent and predictable.

faq.q: Can I use standard deviation if my data is not normally distributed?
faq.a: It can still be used to measure spread. However, other measures might be better depending on the data type.
asks: Does SD need a bell curve?
What if the data is skewed?

faq.q: If I multiply every number by two, what happens to the standard deviation?
faq.a: The standard deviation will also be multiplied by two. It changes proportionally with the data.
asks: If I double the data, double the SD?

faq.a: Yes, standard deviation is a measure of distance, so it cannot be negative. It is always zero or positive.
asks: What is the sign of standard deviation?

faq.q: Does the standard deviation tell me the average of the data?
faq.a: No, the standard deviation does not tell you the average. The mean tells you the average value.
asks: Is SD the same as the mean?
What is the difference between SD and mean?

facts: Standard deviation measures the typical distance of data points from the mean.
A standard deviation of zero means all data points are identical.
The unit for standard deviation is the same as the unit for the original data.
It is calculated using the variance, which is the standard deviation squared.

quiz.say: A set has means of ten with an SD of two. Another set has a mean of ten with an SD of five. Which set is more consistent?

options.show: We cannot tell from the mean
options.say: We cannot tell from the mean

quiz.why: The smaller standard deviation of two shows the data is closer to the mean, meaning it is more consistent.

wrong.0: This is wrong because standard deviation is the specific measure we use to compare spread.
wrong.1: This is wrong because the standard deviation is specifically designed to measure this difference in spread.
wrong.3: This is tempting because the mean is the same, but a larger SD means more spread, not more consistent.

quiz.say: If a data set is {2, 4, 6, 8} and you add five to every number, what is the new standard deviation?

options.show: The standard deviation remains the same
options.say: The standard deviation remains the same

quiz.why: Adding a constant value shifts the data but does not change the spread or the distances between the points.

wrong.0: This confuses the constant added to the data with the measure of spread.
wrong.1: This incorrectly assumes that adding a constant makes all points equal.
wrong.2: This applies a multiplication rule incorrectly to the concept of constant addition.

quiz.say: A set of weights is {10, 10, 10, 10}. What is its standard deviation?
quiz.why: Since every single value is exactly the same, there is no spread, so the standard deviation is zero.

wrong.0: This is wrong because the formula works perfectly fine even when all numbers are identical.
wrong.2: This incorrectly uses the value of the data point instead of measuring the spread around it.
wrong.3: This might be confused with the standard deviation of {1, 2, 3, 4} or another simple calculation.
